Short answer: In modern unified-memory GPUs, bandwidth-bound decoding latency is governed by how well the attention engine can keep the high-bandwidth memory subsystem (HBM + L2) saturated while the compute units (SMs) are busy. Unified memory means the same physical memory is used for model weights, KV cache, and activations; the architecture’s job is to hide the cost of moving data between HBM, L2, L1, shared memory, and LPDDR5X (for off-chip model/weight loading) without stalling the attention kernel.
